items.title: Rise of Magadha & Sources of Information
items.body:
## Magadha Emerges Supreme

- Amid **constant conflicts** between the various **Mahajanapadas**, **Magadha** ultimately emerged as the **largest empire**.
- The **1st dynasty** to rule Magadha was the **Haryanka Dynasty**, founded by **Bimbisara**.
- Magadha was ruled successively by the **Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda** dynasties before the **Mauryas** took over.

## Sources of Information

- **Vedic Texts:** the **Brahmanas** and **Upanishads** refer to various Janapadas and Mahajanapadas.
- **Buddhist Texts:** **Vinaya Pitaka, Sutta Pitaka, Abhidhamma Pitaka** give details of the Mahajanapadas.
- **Jaina Text:** the **Bhagawati Sutra** lists the Mahajanapadas of that time.
- **Archaeology:** **Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW)** pottery found at **Ahichchhatra, Hastinapur, Kausambi, Ujjaini** and other sites.
- **Hathigumpha inscription** at **Udayagiri (near Bhubaneswar, Odisha)** records an **aqueduct** built by **Mahapadma Nanda**.

figure.alt: Timeline chart of Magadha under different dynasties from the Haryanka to the Kanva dynasty
figure.caption: Magadha under different dynasties: Haryanka (544 BCE) → Shishunaga (413 BCE) → Nanda (345 BCE) → Maurya (322 BCE) → Sunga → Kanva.

keyPoints: Magadha became the largest empire among the competing Mahajanapadas.
First ruling dynasty = Haryanka, founded by Bimbisara.
Dynastic order: Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda → Maurya.
Sources: Vedic (Brahmanas/Upanishads), Buddhist (three Pitakas), Jaina (Bhagawati Sutra), and NBPW archaeology.
Hathigumpha inscription at Udayagiri credits Mahapadma Nanda with building an aqueduct.
items.mnemonic: Dynasty order — 'Happy Snakes Never Migrate' = Haryanka, Shishunaga, Nanda, Maurya.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Magadha Dynasties (Introduction; Sources of Information)

items.title: Haryanka Dynasty — Founding & Rulers
items.body:
## The Haryanka Dynasty

- **Capital:** **Rajagriha** (Rajgriha).
- The founder is **debated**, but many scholars credit the **grandfather of Bimbisara**; in practice **Bimbisara** is treated as its true founder.
- The **important rulers** of the dynasty, in order, were **Bimbisara → Ajatashatru → Udayin**.
- The dynasty ended when **Shishunaga**, an Amatya (minister) under the last Haryanka ruler **Nagadasaka**, usurped the throne.
keyPoints: Capital of the Haryanka dynasty was Rajagriha.
Founder debated, but Bimbisara is credited as the effective founder.
Ruler order: Bimbisara → Ajatashatru → Udayin.
Dynasty ended when the minister Shishunaga replaced the last king, Nagadasaka.
items.mnemonic: Haryanka rulers in order — 'BAU' = Bimbisara, Ajatashatru, Udayin.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Magadha Dynasties (Haryanka Dynasty)

items.title: Bimbisara (544–492 BCE)
items.body:
## Bimbisara — The Empire Builder Begins

- **Contemporary** of both **Buddha** and **Mahavira**.
- **Conflict with Avanti:** initially a rival of **Pradyota**, later a friend — he sent his royal physician **Jivaka** to treat Pradyota's jaundice.
- **Conquered Anga** (East Bihar) and its capital **Champa**, vital for trade.
- **Matrimonial alliances** strengthened his position:
  - **1st wife — Mahakoshala** of **Kosala**, brought **Kashi as dowry**.
  - **2nd wife — Lichchhavi princess Chellana** of **Vaishali**, mother of **Ajatashatru**.
  - **3rd wife —** daughter of the **Madra clan (Punjab)**.
keyPoints: Contemporary of Buddha and Mahavira.
Sent physician Jivaka to treat Avanti's ruler Pradyota, turning rivalry into friendship.
Conquered Anga (capital Champa), an important trade region.
Marriage to Mahakoshala of Kosala brought Kashi as dowry.
Marriage to Lichchhavi princess Chellana of Vaishali produced Ajatashatru.
items.mnemonic: Bimbisara's 3 brides = 'KVM' — Kosala (Kashi dowry), Vaishali (Chellana), Madra clan.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Magadha Dynasties (Haryanka Dynasty — Bimbisara)

items.title: Ajatashatru (492–460 BCE)
items.body:
## Ajatashatru — Most Powerful Haryanka Ruler

- The **most powerful** ruler of the dynasty, known for his **military conquests**.
- **Defeated Prasenajit** and annexed **Kosala** and **Kashi**.
- **Annexed Vaishali** after defeating his maternal grandfather, the Lichchhavi chief **Chetak**; also **defeated the Mallas**.
- Introduced war engines — **Mahashilakantaka** (catapult) and **Rathamusala** (mace-fitted chariots).
- Began **fortifying Rajgriha**.
- Arranged the **First Buddhist Council** after Buddha's **Parinirvana**.
keyPoints: Most powerful Haryanka ruler; a great conqueror.
Defeated Prasenajit and annexed Kosala and Kashi.
Annexed Vaishali after defeating his maternal grandfather Chetak; defeated the Mallas.
Introduced war engines: Mahashilakantaka (catapult) and Rathamusala (mace-chariot).
Convened the First Buddhist Council after Buddha's Parinirvana.
items.mnemonic: Ajatashatru's weapons — 'Maha-shila hurls, Ratha-musala crushes' (catapult + mace-chariot).
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Magadha Dynasties (Haryanka Dynasty — Ajatashatru)

items.title: Udayin (460–444 BCE) & the New Capital
items.body:
## Udayin — Founder of Pataliputra

- Under **Udayin**, the new capital was founded at **Pataliputra (modern Patna)**.
- Its site lay at the strategic **confluence of the Ganga and Son rivers**, giving it commercial and defensive advantages.
- Pataliputra would remain the imperial capital of Magadha through the Nanda and Maurya periods.
keyPoints: Udayin (460–444 BCE) founded the new capital at Pataliputra (modern Patna).
Pataliputra sat at the confluence of the Ganga and Son rivers.
The site's river confluence gave trade and defensive advantages.
Pataliputra remained Magadha's capital under later dynasties.
items.mnemonic: 'Udayin Ushered Pataliputra' — U for Udayin, U for the up-river confluence city.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Magadha Dynasties (Haryanka Dynasty — Udayin)

items.title: Shishunaga Dynasty (~413–345 BCE)
items.body:
## The Shishunaga Dynasty

- **Founded by Shishunaga (413 BCE)**, originally an **Amatya (minister)** under **Nagadasaka**, the last Haryanka ruler.
- **Capital** was **temporarily shifted to Vaishali** during his reign.
- **Achievements:**
  - **Conquered Avanti** and integrated it into Magadha, **ending the 100-year rivalry** between the two regions.
- Succeeded by his son **Kalasoka** (also called **Kakavarna**), who presided over the **Second Buddhist Council at Vaishali**.
- Kalasoka was the **last ruler**; he was **murdered by Mahapadma Nanda**, ending the dynasty.

figure.alt: Map of the Magadha Empire 600–321 BCE showing extensions under Bimbisara, Ajatashatru, the Shishunaga and Nanda dynasties
figure.caption: Magadha Empire (600–321 BCE): core under Bimbisara/Ajatashatru, with later extensions by the Shishunaga and Nanda dynasties.

keyPoints: Founded by Shishunaga (413 BCE), formerly minister under the last Haryanka king Nagadasaka.
Capital temporarily shifted to Vaishali.
Conquered Avanti, ending the ~100-year Magadha–Avanti rivalry.
Kalasoka (Kakavarna) held the Second Buddhist Council at Vaishali.
Kalasoka, the last ruler, was murdered by Mahapadma Nanda.
items.mnemonic: Shishunaga kings — 'Shishunaga Starts, Kalasoka Concludes' (only two to remember).
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Magadha Dynasties (Shishunaga Dynasty)

items.title: Nanda Dynasty & Mahapadma Nanda (345–321 BCE)
items.body:
## Rise of the Nandas

- The **Nanda Dynasty** was established by **Mahapadma Nanda** after he overthrew the last Shishunaga king, **Kalasoka**.
- **Brahmanical texts** call Mahapadma Nanda **non-Kshatriya**; **Buddhist texts** describe the Nandas as **Annatakula** (unknown lineage).

## Mahapadma Nanda

- Known as **Ugrasena** because of his **large army**.
- **First empire builder** — claimed the titles **Ekarat** (sole sovereign) and **Sarva-kshatrantaka** (uprooter of Kshatriyas).
- **Added Kalinga** to Magadha and brought back the **image of Jina** as a victory trophy.
- Ran an **effective tax-collection system** and built **irrigation canals** for agriculture.
- **Succeeded by his eight sons**, collectively called the **Navanandas**.

figure.alt: Map of the Nanda Empire around 325 BCE covering much of northern and eastern India
figure.caption: Nanda Empire (c. 325 BCE) — the vast realm consolidated by the Nandas from their capital Pataliputra.

keyPoints: Mahapadma Nanda founded the Nanda dynasty by overthrowing Kalasoka.
Called Ugrasena for his large army; regarded as the first empire builder.
Claimed titles Ekarat (sole sovereign) and Sarva-kshatrantaka (uprooter of Kshatriyas).
Annexed Kalinga and carried off the image of Jina as a trophy.
Succeeded by his eight sons, the Navanandas.
items.mnemonic: Mahapadma = 'Mighty army (Ugrasena), Monarch supreme (Ekarat), Massacres Kshatriyas (Sarva-kshatrantaka)'.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Magadha Dynasties (Nanda Dynasty — Mahapadma Nanda)

items.title: Dhana Nanda & Alexander's Invasion
items.body:
## Dhana Nanda — Last Great Nanda

- The **last significant Nanda ruler**, commanding a **vast army**.
- Called **Agrammes** or **Xandrames** by the Greek historian **Diodorus**.
- Introduced the **Nandopakramani**, a special **measuring standard**.
- He reigned during **Alexander's invasion of northwest India (327–325 BCE)**.
- His unpopularity and heavy taxation set the stage for his overthrow by **Chandragupta Maurya**.
keyPoints: Dhana Nanda was the last significant Nanda ruler, with a vast army.
Greek historian Diodorus called him Agrammes / Xandrames.
Introduced the Nandopakramani, a special measuring standard.
Reigned during Alexander's invasion of NW India (327–325 BCE).
His decline paved the way for the Mauryan takeover.
items.mnemonic: Dhana Nanda = 'Diodorus's Agrammes, During Alexander' — 3 D's link him to the Greeks.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Magadha Dynasties (Nanda Dynasty — Dhana Nanda)

items.title: Transition from the Nandas to the Mauryas
items.body:
## From Nandas to Mauryas

- The Nandas built the **first true pan-north-Indian empire**, but the **unpopular** and heavily taxing **Dhana Nanda** lost legitimacy.
- **Chandragupta Maurya**, guided by **Chanakya (Kautilya)**, overthrew Dhana Nanda around **321 BCE**, founding the **Maurya Dynasty**.
- The transition marks the shift from the Nanda dynasty (**345–321 BCE**) to the **Mauryan Empire (from 322/321 BCE)** — with **Pataliputra** continuing as the imperial capital.
- Full dynastic sequence at Magadha: **Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda → Maurya**.
keyPoints: Dhana Nanda's unpopularity and heavy taxes eroded Nanda legitimacy.
Chandragupta Maurya, aided by Chanakya (Kautilya), overthrew Dhana Nanda c. 321 BCE.
This founded the Maurya dynasty, keeping Pataliputra as capital.
Complete Magadha sequence: Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda → Maurya.
items.mnemonic: Chanakya + Chandragupta = 'CC ends the Nandas' — two C's close the Nanda chapter.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Magadha Dynasties (Nanda Dynasty; dynastic transition)
